claim: The exact QFORM extremal product-law problem can be reduced without loss to one-dimensional support sets of some universal finite diameter; in particular to single unit intervals/centered uniforms.
counterexample: Already for A=I_3, E2=E3=[-1/2,1/2], and J_R=[R^2,R^2+1/4], the x1-fiber is supported on two bands centered near +/-R. Their total length is <1 while their separation tends to infinity. A measure-one finite-fragment E1 containing both bands captures 2 M_R, whereas every measure-one set of any prescribed bounded diameter D captures at most M_R once the band gap exceeds D. The same construction can be symmetric/median-zero.
safe_replacement: Use the exact bang-bang finite-fragment reduction and the zero-loss affine/median normalization, but keep arbitrary fragment separation and support diameter. Any universal proof must be fragment-blind or pay separation by another target-valid mechanism.
